speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of pain during urination. To help me understand what is happening, have you noticed if your right knee or ankle ever becomes red or feels warm to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome).

The clinical picture of a recent lower extremity arthritis followed by urethritis and current monoarthritis in a sexually active adolescent is classic for reactive arthritis. Given the sexual history and symptoms, I will proceed with ordering specific tests to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, Chlamydia DNA, and Rheumatoid Factor.
